Hence the first-order 95% width w_1=3.92·sqrt(Σ_t w_t E_t φ^2/(nD^2)) is an explicit polynomial functional of per-type moments ≤8 (the A1 bound min(m,4p)=8 is attained), w_1, m, n, g and σ^2(·); as m→∞ it reduces to the oracle OLS width 3.92·sqrt(E[ρ^2σ^2]/(nD^2)). Over the response class {|g|≤1 on [0,1]} with σ^2≤r(1−r)/8 the g-term is a PSD quadratic β'Ωβ whose sup is attained on the boundary osc(β_1 r+β_2 r^2)=2 (Chebyshev extreme g=1−8r+8r^2 in all worlds computed).

claims.experimental_consequence: Gives the plan §7.11 a closed-form width criterion at any m (the 'first-order width and population PD margin' closed forms the obstacle asked for); it shows the width tolerance q90≤0.15 cannot be met uniformly over the full class |g|≤1 at (200,128) in the narrow world (sup 0.164) but can for coefficient-bounded g (0.119) — so the response class is a user decision that changes the 128 verdict; it does NOT by itself license m=32 (first-order width 0.144 there while the actual test is 54% non-PD).

claims.statement: Pilot certificate C(pilot; m, G', d_0, w_0): from the 32 (or 128) α=0 counts, per-type moment vector θ̂_t=mean_i U_{1..8}(K_i) (unbiased), question-cluster covariance, delta-method one-sided 95% bounds; fires iff LCB(D)≥d_0 and UCB(sup_{g∈G'} w_1(m))≤w_0 (optional third condition on the A1 PD margin κ(m)=λ_min(E[S_w(m)], N̄(m)), moments ≤4). By derivation: when it fires, D≥d_0 and the first-order width ≤w_0 for every (F,g) in the asymptotic confidence set × G'; the plug-in D̂ is biased downward (D concave in the moments, θ̂ unbiased ⇒ E[D̂]≤D, conservative in the mean). Availability and conditional (two-stage, internal-pilot) size/width validity are to be read from the production-function simulation a2_two_stage_sim.py (4000 reps per linear-g world, 2000 per quadratic-g cell), which was still running at reporting time; single-pilot evaluations show the expected pattern (wide pilot: D̂=0.229 LCB 0.213, UCB(w_1 at 128, full class) 0.122 ⇒ fires; narrow pilot: D̂=0.145 with delta-sd 0.12, half-variance pilot: D̂=0.089 sd 0.20 ⇒ cannot fire).
assumptions: delta-method confidence set (asymptotic, n_t=100); one-sided γ=0.05 per component, Bonferroni over the two components
σ^2≤r(1−r)/8 (no clipping) used inside the certificate; clipping rate reported by the simulation
the simulated design: 50 questions × (2 type-0 + 2 type-1), r iid (no question effect), K128=K32+K96 reuse, η from 16+16 draws, null b_type=0
claims.scope: The certificate's first-order guarantee holds for every F in the stated delta-method confidence set with D≥d_0 and every g∈G'; its availability and its finite-sample validity (size, non-PD, q90 width at the target under reuse) are world-specific simulation quantities for the three Beta worlds and the two g's of the design.
claims.does_not_claim: It does not claim finite-sample size or non-PD control by derivation (no explicit-constant bound exists at n=200 by the tools of A-C3; CE-B1 shows low moments do not determine them); it does not claim the sup over the confidence set is attained at extreme points; it does not claim availability numbers until a2_summary.json exists — the narrow-world unavailability is predicted (pilot noise exceeds the r^2-after-r signal, λ_min(H_w)≈8e-6, check2) but not yet measured by this route.

claims.statement: The explicit-constant finite-sample branch of the certificate is vacuous at the G6 pilot size (100 prefixes per type, m=32) in all three worlds: (i) the Hoeffding/Bonferroni moment box (ε_H=sqrt(ln(640)/200)=0.1797 over 16 moments; 0.1593 over 4) contains the two-point-mass moment vector θ* (μ_{j,t}=μ̂_{1,t}^j) whenever max_{t,j}|μ̂_{j,t}−μ̂_{1,t}^j|≤ε_H, and θ* has D=0 and w_1=∞; this held in 5000/5000 pilots per world (max deviation 0.0069 narrow, 0.0050 half-var, 0.0301 wide), so inf_{box} D=0 and no d_0>0 or finite w_0 can ever be certified; (ii) the per-type DKW band (ε_D=0.148) contains a two-point-per-type world with supports {a,b},{c,d}, a+b=c+d (D=0 exactly) in 20/20 pilots per world (sup-distances 0.025–0.050 narrow, 0.011–0.061 half-var, 0.036–0.080 wide); (iii) matrix Bernstein for ||Ā−Q||<λ_min(Q) with exact σ_1^2 and R from the Beta-binomial law needs n≈1.1e11 (narrow), 8.6e11 (half-var), 6.0e7 (wide), and the whitened version n≈1.2e5–1.4e5 (narrow), 3.5e5–4.1e5 (half-var), 2.5e3–2.8e3 (wide), versus n=200.
assumptions: U_j(K)∈[0,1]; per-type counts iid (Hoeffding applies); Bonferroni over 2 types × 8 orders at γ=0.05
DKW at γ'=0.025 per type on the count CDF; the D=0 family is binomial mixtures with two support points per type and a+b=c+d (then t=κ(r−a)(r−b) exactly)
matrix Bernstein (Tropp) with d=4, s=λ_min(Q), σ_1^2=||E(M̂−Q)^2||, R=max_K||M̂−Q||, computed from the exact Beta-binomial count law of each world
claims.scope: Holds for these three exact constructions at (n_t,m)=(100,32) (Bernstein also at m=128) in the narrow, half-variance and wide Beta worlds; the Hoeffding statement is a proof for every pilot whose max deviation is ≤ε_H (all 15000 simulated); the DKW statement is a proof for each pilot in which a D=0 world was found (60/60).
claims.does_not_claim: It does not claim that no exact finite-sample certificate exists (only that boxes on moments, DKW bands on counts and matrix-Bernstein on the corrected matrix cannot give one at this size), nor that the asymptotic delta-method set of A-C2 has exact coverage.
claims.derivation_md: derivation.md §3 (i)–(iii): Hoeffding box ⊃ θ* ⇒ inf D=0 (θ* degenerate at distinct means ⇒ t exact affine in r); DKW: a+b=c+d makes a quadratic separate the types exactly; Bernstein: n_needed = ln(d/α)(σ_1^2+Rs/3)/(s^2/2).

claims.experimental_consequence: Removes 'rigorous finite-sample certificate with explicit constants at n=200' from the plan's options: any pre-specified pilot rule for §7.11 must be an asymptotic (delta-method / bootstrap) construction whose coverage is simulation-checked, and the non-PD ≤2% tolerance cannot be guaranteed by concentration inequalities — it stays a simulation-calibrated quantity.

what_failed: (1) The finite-sample size/width certificate with explicit constants is unreachable: every exact set (Hoeffding box, DKW band) contains a D=0 world even in the wide world, and matrix Bernstein needs n≥2.5e3–1e11 — proved vacuous (A-C3), so component (A) of the obstacle can only be asymptotic. (2) The first-order width is not an upper bound on q90: the production se is heavy-tailed where the corrected matrix is noise-dominated (m=32 narrow/half-var even at n=20000), so w_1 is necessary, not sufficient, for the width tolerance. (3) The uniform-in-g sup over {|g|≤1} is attained at the Chebyshev extreme and makes the width criterion fail at (200,128) in the narrow world (0.164>0.15) — the class must be coefficient-bounded (user decision). (4) The production-function two-stage simulation (availability per world, false-fire in the half-variance world, reuse vs fresh size) had not finished at the forced reporting time (500/4000 reps per cell); A-C2's decision numbers are therefore missing, and A-C2 is reported as candidate without them.
